title: Tiny-Align - cross-modal alignment framework for ASR-LLM on edge (Raspberry Pi)
problem: Running multi-modal systems combining speech recognition and language models on edge devices like Raspberry Pi is challenging due to memory and compute constraints. Cross-modal alignment typically requires significant computational overhead.
motivation: A lightweight cross-modal alignment framework can enable efficient ASR-LLM integration on edge devices by reducing memory footprint and computational requirements through model compression and efficient alignment mechanisms.
method: Tiny-Align makes automatic speech recognition and language models work together on tiny devices like Raspberry Pi. It uses three techniques: knowledge distillation (transferring what a large model learned into a small one), quantization (storing numbers using fewer bits to save memory), and cross-modal fusion (efficiently combining speech and language outputs). These techniques are designed to fit within the severe memory and computing limits of edge devices.
key_novelty: Framework for combining automatic speech recognition with language models on tiny devices like Raspberry Pi.
contributions: Lightweight ASR-LLM alignment framework for edge deployment
50× training speedup through optimized algorithms and compression
Demonstration of multi-modal AI feasibility on Raspberry Pi
limitations: Model compression may degrade accuracy for complex linguistic phenomena, and extreme speedup claims suggest possible benchmarking limitations or unrealistic baselines.
